## The contract (pinned; A is coding against this verbatim)

src/calc.js is an ES module whose every export line starts with `export ` at column 0; the build strips that prefix and inlines the result as a classic script. It exports:
- DEFAULTS: { key: { value:number, unit, label, group:'blocks'|'walls'|'concrete'|'steel'|'prices'|'wastage', rationale, source, sourceUrl:string|null, confidence:'Certain'|'Likely'|'Guessing', lastChecked:'YYYY-MM-DD' } }
- ASSUMPTION_NOTES: [ { key, value:string, rationale, source, confidence, lastChecked } ]  (construction system, concrete grade, the "list every space" rule — show these as read-only text at the top of the assumptions panel)
- LIMITS: { floors:[1,4], wallHeightM:[2.4,4.5], roomSideM:[1,20], rooms:[1,40], areaM2:[30,1500] }  (use for input min/max/step attributes)
- SAMPLE_HOUSE: { floors, wallHeightM, rooms:[{name,lengthM,widthM}] }
- generateRooms(areaM2) → rooms[]  (throws plain-English Error outside LIMITS)
- validateHouse(house) → house  (throws plain-English Error)
- estimate(house, overrides={}) → { inputs:{ floors, wallHeightM, roomCount, floorAreaM2, builtUpAreaM2, extWallLengthM, intWallLengthM, grossWallAreaM2, netWallAreaM2, extWallAreaM2, intWallAreaM2 }, elements:{ footings, groundSlab, columns, beams, slabs, wallsExternal, wallsInternal — each { label, concreteM3, steelKg, blocks, wastagePct, costOmr } }, totals:{ blocks, blocksExternal, blocksInternal, concreteM3, steelKg, steelTonnes, costOmr, costBlocksOmr, costConcreteOmr, costSteelOmr }, assumptionsUsed:[ { key, label, value, unit, defaultValue, overridden, source, sourceUrl, confidence, lastChecked } ], notes:[string] }
  overrides = { [DEFAULTS key]: number } — only include keys the user actually changed. estimate throws a plain-English Error on bad input; catch it and show the message in #results-error.

## src/page.html
A complete HTML5 document (lang="en", viewport meta, <title>House Material Estimator</title>), all CSS in one <style>, all JS in one <script> at the end, no external assets of any kind. It contains exactly two markers on their own lines:
- `<!--CALC-->` — the build replaces it with `<script>` + calc.js (export prefixes stripped) + `</script>`. Your page script must come AFTER it and call the globals estimate, DEFAULTS, etc. directly.
- `<!--BUILDLOG-->` — the build replaces it with `<script type="application/json" id="build-log">[...records...]</script>`. Your page script reads and JSON.parses that element and renders section 2 from it (records: { order:number, agent, model, round, startedAt, finishedAt?, prompt, report?, outcome? }; sort by order then round; the order field can be like 4 for both "04a" and "04b" so ALSO sort by the record's `file` field which the build adds as the filename stem, e.g. "04a-builder"). A record without report yet renders as "in progress".
Section 2 intro must include, in plain English: this page was built by a team of AI agents from the owner's central agent library, each a small text file describing one job; a main session (the "orchestrator") ran the dev-lead commander's playbook — spec → research and screen design → two builders in parallel → verifier → code review, with bounded fix loops; and the honest note that in a cloud session the harness allows only one level of agents, so the main session dispatched the crew itself instead of dev-lead doing it. The org diagram lists the distinct agents from the records with their model badge. Also show, per record, duration in minutes when finishedAt exists.
Everything the estimator shows on screen comes from estimate()'s return value — format numbers with thousands separators and units, steel as tonnes with 1 decimal (kg in a title attribute), OMR with 0 decimals, m³ with 1 decimal. Render the assumptions panel from DEFAULTS grouped by `group` in DEFAULTS order; each row's input is the override source; a "reset" per row and a "reset all" control. Show source as a link when sourceUrl exists, else plain text; show confidence as a small badge and lastChecked as text. Notes from result.notes render under the results. Rooms: table/cards with add-row and remove-row; the m² shortcut per the UI spec; all inputs constrained by LIMITS; numeric parsing tolerant of blanks (blank → error from validate, never NaN). Load-sample fills every input from SAMPLE_HOUSE; calculate reads the DOM and calls estimate(house, overrides). No innerHTML with unescaped user or record text — escape it (prompts and reports contain angle brackets and backticks).

## scripts/build.mjs
Node ESM, no dependencies. Reads src/page.html, src/calc.js, every docs/build-log/*.json (sorted by filename; add `file` = filename stem to each record), performs the two replacements, and writes index.html. Fails loudly (non-zero exit, clear message) if a marker is missing, calc.js has an `import` line, or a build-log file isn't valid JSON. Prints one line: the output path, size in KB, and record count. Must be idempotent (same inputs → byte-identical output) because the verify recipe runs `git diff --exit-code -- index.html`.

## Prove it before you report
1. `node scripts/build.mjs` succeeds with the stub swapped in if src/calc.js isn't there yet — but the committed state must use the real src/calc.js if it exists when you finish; re-run the build against the real file if it has appeared.
2. `node scripts/smoke.mjs` passes at 1440 and 390 (it clicks load-sample, then calculate, reads [data-result="blocks-total"], and fails on console errors or horizontal scroll). If it fails, fix the page, not the smoke test.
3. Check dark mode renders (prefers-color-scheme) at least by reading your CSS; and that section 2 renders the existing docs/build-log records (there are several already).
If src/calc.js still doesn't exist when you finish, say so and report the smoke result against the stub.

Your final message (plain English, under 25 lines): files written, build output line, smoke result at both widths, whether the real calc.js or the stub was used, any place you deviated from the UI spec and why, and any concern for the reviewer.
